narrative.overview:
A control room at the edge of the ice: deep polar blue, seafoam for the actions that move work forward, ice blue for information and focus. Zimuarr is a dense desktop tool with clear subtitle classifications and budget rulers. Typography is clean, panels are flat, and there is no decorative photography or cinematic gradient. It is dark-first: dark is the only colour mode.

The tokens live in [`panda.config.ts`](panda.config.ts), and components use them only through Panda, with `strictTokens` refusing raw values. This file describes how they are used. The frontmatter mirrors the Panda config; when the two disagree, the config wins and this file is refreshed. The claim page at `/setup` is the first built surface. The guidance for components not built yet (navigation, tables, dialogs, badges, toasts) is the direction their surfaces build to.

[Product context](PRODUCT.md) and the [surface briefs](.impeccable/surfaces/) define behaviour. The mockups in [docs/design](docs/design/) guide composition and visual character; each brief records the raster corrections for its board's incidental text. Generated raster pixels are visual guidance: they never override named tokens or product requirements.
keyCharacteristics: Flat `surface` panels on the `background` page, separated by 1px borders, not shadows.
One solid seafoam action per task area; ice blue only for information, links and focus.
Fields recessed into the page colour, bounded by a brighter control border.
Public Sans for everything read, Roboto Mono for codes and operational numbers.
Quiet operational screens; motion only as feedback.

rules.name: The Ice-Blue Signal Rule
rules.body: `secondary` marks information, links and keyboard focus. A primary button keeps its Seafoam fill on hover rather than turning ice blue.

rules.name: The No Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: A state is never told by colour alone: errors, statuses and badges always carry a word, and badges an icon too.

rules.name: The 16px Field Rule
rules.body: Text inside a field is never smaller than body size (16px), since iOS zooms in on smaller input text. A field that echoes a code, such as the setup token, uses the mono face at body size, not the 13px `code` style.

rules.name: The Flat Panel Rule
rules.body: No repeated card drop shadows and no glowing status dots: a panel is a `surface` fill with a 1px `border`.

rules.name: The Recessed Field Rule
rules.body: A field is a `background` well inside its `surface` panel, so its fill and its `control-border` both mark it out; no field shares its panel's fill.

dos: **Do** use only the Panda tokens; `strictTokens` refuses raw values, and DESIGN.md is refreshed from the config, never the other way round.
**Do** keep welcome and experience screens expressive and operational screens quiet.
**Do** treat permissions, status transitions and budget arithmetic as behaviour the server supplies.
**Do** use the [demo fixtures](tests/fixtures/demo-fixtures.json) for stable visual tests, then substitute real server data.
**Do** follow each surface brief's raster corrections instead of copying a board's accidental labels or extra actions.
**Do** build on Panda CSS and Ark UI, without adding a competing component library.
donts: **Don't** blend the edbfi apps into one theme: this palette and type hierarchy are zimuarr's, on every route.
**Don't** add drop shadows to panels or cards, or glows to status dots.
**Don't** put imagery behind data, text fields or tables.
